title: New Mexico hunting licenses, draws, and fees
intro: Public-land deer and elk licenses are issued through the NMDGF big-game draw. A Game-Hunting License is required before most tags. Fees below are the 2026–27 amounts published by NMDGF. Confirm before you apply or pay.

whereToBuy.title: Online
whereToBuy.body: Apply for the draw and buy OTC licenses at https://onlinesales.wildlife.dgf.nm.gov/.

whereToBuy.title: License vendor
whereToBuy.body: License vendors sell OTC licenses and can help with draw applications. A vendor fee applies.

whereToBuy.title: Big-game draw
whereToBuy.body: Deer, elk, pronghorn, and other big-game public licenses are a random draw (no preference points). Application deadline for 2026 was March 18; results April 22.

whereToBuy.title: Over the counter
whereToBuy.body: Game-Hunting License, turkey, and private-land-only deer/pronghorn licenses sell OTC after the draw window.

whereToBuy.title: Phone / mail
whereToBuy.body: NMDGF Licensing can take phone applications. Confirm current phone sales at wildlife.dgf.nm.gov.

deadlines.name: License year
deadlines.detail: 2026–27 licenses generally run April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027.

fees.item: Draw application fee (included in draw license)

preferencePoints: New Mexico does not use preference points for big-game draws. Each application is random.
Quota shares for most deer and elk hunts are approximately 84% resident, 10% nonresident, 6% outfitter.
Nonresidents are ineligible for antlerless elk and most WMA-only draw hunts.
